To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the encapsulated probiotic cells (L. plantarum) were found alive even at 72°C, 90 s, and pH 6.5, and the survival was found higher with hybrid hydrogel beads.

the survival of probiotic Lactobacillus cells was enhanced by using the encapsulation method with hybrid hydrogel beads (alginate-soy protein) and that the survival of encapsulated cells was found higher in the hybrid hydrogel bead than in alginate bead.

the survival of probiotics encapsulated in the hybrid hydrogel (alginate-soy protein) was significantly enhanced in acidic conditions (p. 3 and 6.6) and in thermal treatment (72°C) and the survival of probiotic was higher in the hybrid hydrogels containing alginate-soy-protein (8:1 w/w).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel probiotic hydrogel beads for the incorporation in the fruit juices.
the preparation of hydrogel beads with the potential for use in the food industry to incorporate probiotics in food and beverage products without affecting their viability.
the preparation, characterization, and evaluation of the survival of probiotic bacteria encapsulated in hybrid hydrogel beads for the development of a new probiotic beverage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid hydrogel (alginate-soy protein) beads can be used to enhance the survival and stability of probiotic cells in mango juice.
the encapsulated probiotic cells were protected against heat processing and bile salt, and they could survive in the mango juice during storage.
encapsulation of probiotic bacteria (L. plantarum) with alginate-soy isolate (SA-SIP) hydrogel beads can enhance the survival of probiotics during heat treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
encapsulated probiotics in hybrid hydrogel beads could be used in mango juice as an effective probiotic delivery vehicle.
encapsulation in hydrogel beads could enhance the survival and stability of probiotic bacteria during thermal treatment in mango juice.
the hybrid hydrogel bead containing L. plantarium was successfully incorporated into mango juice and the survival of probiotic was maintained even after thermal processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hybrid alginate-soy isolate beads can be used for the delivery of probiotic bacteria in mango juice.
the hybrid hydrogel bead containing alginate and SPI can be used as a delivery system for probiotics in mango juice to enhance the survival rate of probiotics under heat treatment.
the encapsulation of probiotic cells in hybrid hydrogel beads could be a good approach for their survival during thermal processing.
